newsitem.title: USA: IBM touts SET Internet security protocol.
newsitem.headline: IBM touts SET Internet security protocol.

text.p: A top Internet executive with International Business Machines Corp said Wednesday that electronic commerce on the World Wide Web cannot succeed unless businesses adopt existing industry standards for electronic transactions, particularly the Secure Electronic Transaction (SET) protocol.

Speaking at the Internet Commerce Expo, IBM Internet Division General Manager Irving Wladawsky-Berger said analysts believe revenues from electronic commerce will double to $2 billion this year and reach $1 trillion by the year 2010.

"Of course, none of that will happen unless the commercial infrastructure can make payments, property rights and privacy at least as secure as the traditional business environment," the IBM executive said in a keynote speech. "If there is one killer technology, it is security, because without security, electronic commerce and business in general are dead."

Wladawsky-Berger touted the SET protocol pioneered by Mastercard and Visa International as a measure to secure credit and debit card payments, saying the industry standard made electronic commerce lower-risk than traditional credit card transactions.
On Wednesday, IBM also used the Internet Commerce Expo to announce the launch of a new version of the Net.Commerce merchant server, calling it the first product of its kind to use the SET protocol.
